title: Diabetic Emergencies
content_markdown:
# Diabetic Emergencies

- Assess blood glucose level.

#### BGL < 4 mmol/L

- If symptomatic, but conscious and laryngeal reflexes intact: 
- Oral glucose (via gel or food).

- If decreased LOC: 
- Glucose 10% IV (repeat once if required).
- If no IV access available: 
- Glucagon IM.
- Consider the cause of the hypoglycaemia (e.g. infection, seizure, insulin overdose, etc.) as this may necessitate medical review.
- Ensure oral intake of carbohydrate if patient is not transported.
**Note:** Recovery may be slow if hypoglycaemia has been prolonged or severe.

#### BGL > 15 mmol/L

- Fluid replacement as per CMG 14 Shock and Hypoperfusion.
- If shocked and hypotensive: IV fluid resuscitation (as per CMG 14).

#### Insulin Pumps

- In the event of hypoglycaemia, consider suspending administration **if the patient or a carer on scene is able to assist in doing so. **
- If there is no assistance on scene do not attempt to alter settings.

Whether suspended or not, **do not remove the pump** – transport with pump in situ. No special management is required as long as the pump and infusion site are protected.

Glucose.text: Glucose 10% IV: Formula: 0.25 (2.5ml)/kg Preparation: 50g in 500ml Dose: 0.75ml/kg Volume: 7.5ml
Treatment of hypoglycaemia (BGL <4mmol/L) when patient is unable to eat or drink.
Hypertonic glucose solution – containing 0.1g dextrose per ml
10% glucose – in 250ml in collapsible plastic flask
Treat hypoglycaemia (BGL <4mmol/L, and patient unable to eat/drink)
Patients who respond to glucose 10% should eat, to prevent later development of further hypoglycaemia.
Treatment of hypoglycaemia (BGL <4mmol/L) when patient is conscious and able to swallow
1 x tube of 15g glucose orally  May be repeated once after 15 minutes if BGL still < 4 mmol/L, and level of consciousness still altered Total maximum dose 30g glucose

##### Type

Hypertonic glucose solution – containing 0.1g dextrose per ml

##### Presentations

10% glucose – in 250ml in collapsible plastic flask

##### Actions

Glucose is the main energy source for the body cells, especially the brain. 
 Onset: 30 – 60 seconds. 

#### Uses

Treat hypoglycaemia (BGL <4mmol/L, and patient unable to eat/drink)

#### Adverse Effects

- Tissue necrosis if allowed to escape from the vein

- Hyperglycaemia / hyperosmolality

#### Contraindications

Known hypersensitivity

#### Pregnancy and Breastfeeding

##### Pregnancy

- Safe to use

##### Breastfeeding

- Safe to use

#### Doses

##### Adult and Paediatric

- Up to 2.5ml/kg (0.25g/kg) slowly over 5 minutes 
- Continue to check patency of vein
- May repeat dose once, if LOC or BGL has not improved.

#### Special Notes

- Patients who respond to glucose 10% should eat, to prevent later development of further hypoglycaemia.
- Recheck BGL following treatment.

##### Type

Oral glucose gel [no schedule]

##### Presentations

37.5g tube containing 15g glucose

##### Actions

- Glucose is the main energy source for the body’s cells, especially the brain 

- Glucose preparation is rapidly absorbed from oral / buccal mucosa 

- Causes an increase in blood glucose concentration

Onset: approximately 10 minutes.

#### Uses

Treatment of hypoglycaemia (BGL <4mmol/L) when patient is conscious and able to swallow

#### Contraindications

Impaired or absent swallow / gag reflex

#### Pregnancy and Breastfeeding

##### Pregnancy

- Safe to use

##### Breastfeeding

- Safe to use

#### Doses

##### Adult and Paediatric

- 1 x tube of 15g glucose orally 
- May be repeated once after 15 minutes if BGL still < 4 mmol/L, and level of consciousness still altered
- Total maximum dose 30g glucose
- Not to be given IV or IM.

#### Special Notes

- Patients should swallow the entire contents of the tube (where possible) to maximise the rise in BGL.
- Patients who respond to oral glucose gel should eat to prevent later development of further hypoglycaemia.
- Re-check BGL following treatment.
- Gel liquefies when over 30\xb0C (it is still useable). Re-cool if possible.

#### Indications

- Altered level of consciousness.
- Suspected stroke.
- Post seizure.
- Diabetic.

#### Procedure

- Place strip into monitor. The glucometer will auto turn on.

- Select a finger and clean with an alcohol swab, allow finger to dry.

- Using a lancet, pierce the skin and squeeze a small amount of blood from the wound.

- Dispose of the used lancet appropriately.

- Place a sample of blood on the test strip until the BGL device beeps and a countdown appears.

- Apply a Band-Aid to the wound.

- Wait for the test result and record the BGL measurement.

- Dispose of the used test strip appropriately.

#### Specific Notes

- A “LO” or “HI” reading indicates a BGL <1.1mmol /L or >27.8 mmol/L.
- Presence of ^ arrow does not indicate ketones, this signals a high BGL reading. Ketone testing requires a different testing strip, this testing method will not give any indication of ketones.

Glucagon.text: Formula: weight <20kg = 0.5 IU Preparation: 1IU in 1ml Dose: 0.5 IU Volume: 0.5ml
Vial containing 1 International Unit of glucagon as a dry powder, with a syringe containing 1ml of diluting solution

##### Type

Pancreatic hormone [S4]

##### Presentations

Vial containing 1 International Unit of glucagon as a dry powder, with a syringe containing 1ml of diluting solution

##### Actions

Causes the liver to metabolise stores of glycogen to glucose, resulting in a rise in the blood glucose level. 
 Only effective if liver glycogen is available. 
 Onset IM: 5 – 20 minutes 

#### Uses

Treatment of hypoglycaemia (BGL <4mmol/L) when patient is unable to eat or drink.

#### Adverse Effects

Very rare

- Nausea and vomiting

- Very occasionally, hypersensitivity

#### Contraindications

Known hypersensitivity

#### Pregnancy and Breastfeeding

##### Pregnancy

- Safe to use

##### Breastfeeding

- Safe to use

#### Doses

##### Adults

- 1 International Unit (IU) – IM 
- Single dose only.

##### Paediatric

- Weight <20kg (approx. 5yrs): 0.5 IU – IM 
- Single dose only.

- Weight >20kg: 1 IU – IM 
- Single dose only.

#### Special Notes

- Patients who respond to glucagon should eat, to prevent later development of further hypoglycaemia.
- Recheck BGL following treatment.
